docs.title: Project Overview
docs.text:
The game is a cooperative third-person action-investigation game in which a team of SCAR operatives enters dangerous environments to investigate unexplained phenomena, identify anomalies, complete objectives, and survive increasingly chaotic encounters.

Each mission presents players with a partially unknown situation. The team must gather information, investigate the environment, determine what is happening, and respond appropriately.

Not every threat should be solved with gunfire.

Some anomalies may be hostile creatures. Others may manipulate the environment, deceive players, create supernatural events, alter reality, or generate escalating waves of enemies.

The combination of procedural missions, investigation, unpredictable anomalies, combat, SCAR-issued equipment, and multiplayer chaos should make each mission feel different.

Players do not select from a roster of predefined heroes. Instead, each player builds their own SCAR operative through appearance customization, equipment selection, and mission preparation.

docs.title: What is SCAR?
docs.text:
SCAR is the temporary title of the game in development. It is derived from the primary focus of the game The U.N.S.C.A.R. (United Nations Supernatural Containment And Response) Initiative. They are an organization formed by the United Nations after the first world-wide encounter with supernatural forces in 2020, when an interdimensional god of chaos plunged the world into a time of pure chaos for roughly 40 years. Thanks to the help of an unknown group of super-powered individuals often called "The Squatters", they defeated the threat and reversed time so that only 8 months had passed.

Following these events the United Nations met and determined that there needed to be a governing body over all responses to supernatural forces. They created The U.N.S.C.A.R. Initiative. After its creation, the initiative decided that it was best for the public to have no memory of the chaotic events of 2020, so they erased the memory of these events across the world. The world now simply remembers it as a global pandemic.

docs.title: 0: Brief Project Overview
docs.text: This project uses Godot and Kotlin. Godot is the game engine, and Kotlin is the language we are programming in. To program in Kotlin, we will be using the JVM-plugin for Godot. This page will provide resources to help you easily learn what you need to start working on this project.

docs.title: 1: Tutorials
docs.text:
Before working on the actual project, start by following these tutorials.

The following tutorials are in the recommended order to follow before starting work on this project

docs.title: A: GD-Quest
docs.text: GD-Quest is a strong starting point for someone who has never programmed. It teaches variables, conditions, loops, functions, and other fundamentals through interactive exercises. The examples use GDScript, not Kotlin, but the programming concepts transfer.

docs.title: B: Intro to Godot
docs.text: You may follow this Youtube tutorial series, or navigate through these docs. The docs and tutorial series will likely include GD-Script programming. This is fine, you will learn Kotlin later. If you’ve used Godot before you may skip this step

docs.title: C: Learn Kotlin
docs.text: Kotlin Koans is a series of exercises to get you familiar with the Kotlin syntax and some idioms. Each exercise is created as a failing unit test, and your job is to make it pass. Don’t skip this unless you’ve used Kotlin before.

docs.title: D: Godot JVM
docs.text: Read the Godot JVM documentation. Now that you’ve learned how to program in Kotlin, and navigate Godot, the concepts should feel familiar here.

docs.title: 2: Environment Setup
docs.text:
You’ve likely already downloaded Godot, assuming you’ve followed the tutorials listed above. You very likely have not downloaded the Godot JVM plugin though.

We will be using the community edition of the IntelliJ IDEA.

docs.title: Setup Instructions:
docs.text:
1. Start by downloading the IDE linked above.
  2. Once it has been downloaded, navigate to the Plugins within the IDE. Search for “Godot Kotlin/JVM”. The plugin is published by “Utopia-Rise”.
    • Install the plugin to your IDE.
  3. Now search for “GitHub” in the plugins.
    • If this plugin isn’t installed already, please install it.

docs.title: 3: GitHub
docs.text: Create an account on GitHub. Share your account user name with Thomas, and he will add you as a contributor to the project.

docs.title: 4: Clone Repository
docs.text:
Navigate to your IntelliJ IDE.  You will likely see an option to clone a repository, click this option.  

Then you will be prompted for a link, now navigate to the GitHub repository, copy the link, and paste it into IntelliJ.

The branch should now be loading, it may take a bit for it to build. You will probably need to link your GitHub account to the IDE.

docs.title: 5: Start a Task
docs.text:
On the GitHub, navigate to the Issues section.  You will see multiple tasks that you can pick up. You will see a labels section, click the label “good first issue”

Find an issue with that label. Now you should assign the issue to yourself, and create a branch for you work on.  When creating a branch make sure you follow this naming scheme:

“{item type}/scar-{issue#}-brief-title”

Make sure you don’t have any special characters, only letters, numbers and “-” dashes.

In the example below it results to: “issue/scar-1-create-initial-project-structure”

There are different types of work items in this project, the most common are:

  • Standalone
    • A single unit of work linked to nothing else.  Worked on by one person.
    • Branches start with “issue/”
  • Story
    • A broad feature that is written from the perspective of a user/player.
    • Contains multiple tasks linked to it.
    • Branches start with “story/”
  • Task
    • A work item linked to a feature.
    • Branches start with “task/”
  • Bug
    • Something is broken or not working as intended and needs to be fixed.
    • Branches start with “bug/” 
  • Tech-Debt
    • A previous approach to an implementation was poor, or doesn’t follow good practice, and it needs to get fixed.
    • Branches start with “techdebt/"
  • Spike
    • Something needs to be investigated before work can be started.
    • Branches start with “spike/“.

docs.title: Investigation
docs.text:
Players should rarely have complete information when a mission begins.

The team must:

  • Explore unfamiliar environments.
  • Search for evidence.
  • Identify unusual environmental behavior.
  • Determine what type of anomaly they are dealing with.
  • Understand the rules governing an encounte
  • Decide how to respond.
  • Adapt when their assumptions are proven wrong.

The goal is to make discovery itself part of the gameplay.

docs.title: Chaos
docs.text:
Chaos is a core identity of the game.

The game should create situations where carefully made plans can rapidly fall apart.

Examples include:

  • An unexpected enemy appearing.

  • An anomaly changing the environment.

  • A normally safe area becoming dangerous.

  • A player accidentally triggering an event.

  • A quiet investigation turning into a firefight.

  • A small enemy encounter escalating into a horde.

  • Players becoming separated.

  • Environmental hazards interfering with combat.

  • An anomaly behaving differently than expected.

  • Equipment being used in an unintended but effective way.

Chaos should not mean randomness for its own sake.

The ideal experience is:

Players make a plan → the game disrupts the plan → players improvise → the situation escalates → players recover or fail.

docs.title: Helldivers 2
docs.text:
Helldivers 2 serves as one of the best examples of pure chaos in a video game.

Every interaction has a chance to bring great success or great destruction.

docs.title: Resident Evil Requiem & Resident Evil 4 Remake
docs.text: RE4 & RE9 both find a great balance between action and horror. The movement and combat of this game will be heavily inspired by these two games due to its ability to provide enough speed for players to feel like a seasoned agent, but still being very grounded into reality.

docs.title: Phasmaphobia
docs.text:
Phasmaphobia allows players to investigate an unknown threat, and use deduction to decide what that threat it.

The aspect of investigation displayed in Phasmaphobia inspires a core part of how players are able to contain supernatural threats in this game.

docs.title: SCP Foundation
docs.text:
The SCP Foundation is the primary inspiration for the lore and context of the game.

This game will make the players feel like they are a field agent in an organization very similar to the SCP Foundation.
